**Michelle Jones-Watson**, most commonly known as **MJ**, is a fictionalcharacter portrayed by Zendaya in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) film franchise, an original character within the media franchise that pays homage to Mary Jane "MJ" Watson, main love interest of Spider-Man in comic books and various media.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Zendaya1-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-4)

She is depicted as a smart, snarky classmate of Peter Parker in _Spider-Man: Homecoming_ (2017), and in _Spider-Man: Far From Home_ (2019) becomes his love interest as well as correctly guessing Peter is Spider-Man.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Geek-5) She returns in _Spider-Man: No Way Home_ (2021), helping Peter, Ned Leeds, and Doctor Strange to capture multiple villains that have entered their universe from the multiverse, due to a failed spell to make the world forget about Mysterio revealing that Peter was Spider-Man. Her romantic involvement in Peter's personal life would eventually be undone due to Strange's casting of a spell that permanently erased the world's memory of Peter's civilian persona, including the loss of his previous bonds he forged with his friends, loved ones, and allies.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-6) MJ returns in _Spider-Man: Brand New Day_ (2026), living a normal life after forgetting Peter. However, she is quickly caught in the middle of Peter's conflict with Jean Grey, where she discovers Spider-Man's identity and appears to regain her memories of Peter by the movie's end.
The character has received positive reviews, and Zendaya has been praised as a strong female supporting cast member, receiving the Saturn Award for Best Supporting Actress for her acting in _Far From Home_.

## Creation and concept
[edit]
> She has a really cool wardrobe, really funny, lots of literary nods. I like the idea that she's a real reader and bookish. She always has a big pile of books she's carrying around, which I picked and obsessed over.
According to _Spider-Man: Homecoming_ co-screenwriter John Francis Daley, Michelle was intended as a reinvention of Mary Jane Watson.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-yahoo!-8) While her nickname reveal was an homage to the supporting character within the comic books and other Spider-Man media, Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige confirmed she is an original Marvel Cinematic Universe character.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-IGN-9) Feige added: "Peter's had a lot of friends over the years in the comics, and a lot of schoolmates and characters he's interacted with. It wasn't just Mary Jane Watson; it wasn't just Gwen Stacy; it wasn't just Harry Osborn. So we were very interested in the other characters, and that's where Liz came from and that's where the version of the character Michelle came from."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-DOG-10)Jon Watts, director of _Spider-Man: Homecoming_, _Spider-Man: Far From Home_ and _Spider-Man: No Way Home_, likened the character to Ally Sheedy's Allison Reynolds from _The Breakfast Club_ (1985) and Linda Cardellini's Lindsay Weir from _Freaks and Geeks_ (1999–2000).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-\film-7)

## Creation and concept
The character's full name is Michelle Jones-Watson, which was first revealed in _Spider-Man: No Way Home_. Until that point, she had been referred to once as Michelle and primarily known by the nickname MJ; although the name "Michelle Jones" had been used in an article by _Variety_, quickly spreading among the press and fans through citogenesis, the name was not used in any official media until _No Way Home_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-full_name-1) Zendaya revealed during an interview in 2026, that there was a scene filmed for _No Way Home_ which would have revealed why MJ dropped the "Jones" part of her name, but it was cut from the final film.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-11)

## Portrayal and characterization
[edit]
Zendaya portrays the character in the MCU.
MJ is portrayed by actress Zendaya in the Marvel Cinematic Universe as a classmate of Peter Parker at Midtown School of Science and Technology and a teammate on the academic decathlon team. She is depicted as politically active with critical views, and a loner who claims to eschew friendship.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Mashable-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-CheatSheet-13) Zendaya described the character as "very dry, awkward, intellectual".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-HollywoodReporter-14) This sometimes manifests itself in the form of deadpan sarcasm,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Polygon-17) as when she calls Peter and Ned "losers" for ogling his crush, Liz, from afar.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-CheatSheet-13) Among her unusual hobbies is attending detention simply to "sketch people in crisis."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Mashable-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-CheatSheet-13)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-WhatCulture-18)

## Portrayal and characterization
Unlike previous supporting female characters within _Spider-Man_ films, such as Mary Jane Watson from the Sam Raimi trilogy and Gwen Stacy from the _Amazing Spider-Man_ films, MJ is neither a romantic interest nor a damsel in distress at the beginning of her character arc. Instead, the character Liz was created initially for the role of romantic interest in a way that tied into Parker's conflict with the Vulture.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-19)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Geek-5)
In the third film, she is rescued from a fall by Andrew Garfield's incarnation of Spider-Man, prompting an emotional moment for that Spider-Man, in light of his failure to save Gwen Stacy from a similar fate in _The Amazing Spider-Man 2_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-rescue-20)

## Fictional character biography
[edit]
In 2016, Michelle, commonly known as MJ, is introduced as a student at Midtown School of Science and Technology and enjoys mocking her classmates, including Peter Parker. She is a member of the Academic Decathlon team and attends a competition in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), during which they win, although she notices Peter's disappearance. At the Washington Monument, she witnesses Spider-Man's arrival. After Liz Allan leaves the school, she is offered Allan's role of Captain of the team by Roger Harrington. She begins to open up more with teammates, such as Peter and Ned Leeds, secretly considering them as her friends.
In 2018, MJ is a victim of the Blip,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-21) before being restored to life in 2023.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-22) In 2024, MJ attends the school-sponsored trip to Europe, where her affections are sought out by both Peter and Brad Davis. When she deduces Peter's identity as Spider-Man, MJ helps discover Mysterio's hero fraud, as he was the one who staged the Elemental invasion. In London, MJ, Ned, Betty Brant, and Flash Thompson are met by Happy Hogan and take cover from Mysterio's drones after they get targeted. After Mysterio is defeated, MJ embraces Peter. Soon after returning home, MJ and Peter begin a relationship and have their first date by swinging in the city. Afterwards, they witness _TheDailyBugle.net_'sJ. Jonah Jameson releasing a doctored video of Mysterio and Spider-Man, claiming that Spider-Man is responsible for the Battle of London (during which Mysterio was killed) and exposing his identity as Peter Parker.

## Fictional character biography
### Multiversal invasion
[edit]
MJ is immediately surrounded by people asking her if she is Spider-Man's girlfriend, but is picked up by Peter and swung back to his apartment, where she meets Peter's aunt May. She is eventually interrogated and taken to custody by the Department of Damage Control. MJ, Peter, and Ned then become infamous, resulting in all their college applications being rejected.
MJ and Ned are found by Stephen Strange and brought to the New York Sanctum to help Peter track down individuals from alternate universes who were brought to theirs after a spell went wrong. They are instructed by Peter to keep watch over Strange's mystical box as he tries to help the individuals be cured of their villainous traits. At Ned's grandmother's house, MJ encourages Ned to use Strange's sling ring to try to locate Peter. Ned successfully opens a portal, but the two are instead met with an alternate version of Peter (later dubbed "Peter-Three"). Ned tries again, only to locate another alternate version of Peter (later dubbed "Peter-Two"). MJ and Ned go to Midtown's rooftop and comfort Peter, who had just witnessed the Green Goblin kill May. They then introduce him to his two variants, who provide advice, and join them in Midtown's laboratory.
MJ and Ned are attacked by Lizard after Ned is unable to close the portal from Midtown to the Statue of Liberty, although Peter comes to their aid. MJ and Ned escape onto the Statue and Ned opens another portal, this time leading them to Strange. MJ falls off of the statue after a pumpkin bomb from the Goblin detonates on the mystical box, destabilizing the spell once more and threatening the fabric of reality. Peter tries to save her but is whisked away by the Goblin, and Peter-Three, who lost his own girlfriend, Gwen Stacy, in a similar manner, takes notice and saves her. Peter tells MJ and Ned that Strange would recast the spell on his request to erase him from everyone's memory in order to send the multiversal visitors back home. MJ confesses her love for Parker and they kiss passionately before the spell takes effect.
Weeks later, MJ greets Ned at her shop, both having been accepted into MIT, and meets Peter, who considers reintroducing himself, but ultimately decides against it, wishing to not involve her and Ned in his life again to protect them from harm.

## Fictional character biography
### Multiversal invasion
After graduating from MIT, MJ and Ned rent an apartment together in New York. During the housewarming party, MJ runs into Peter, who had followed Ned into the apartment and mingled with the crowd. He had brought flowers with him, passing them off as a welcome gift and giving them to her, pretending to be a neighbor. Peter watches her from afar until he sees her with her new boyfriend, which compels him to leave.
Some time later, Spider-Man appears at MJ's apartment, saying she is in danger urging her to come with him, to which she reluctantly obliges. On a rooftop, MJ asks Spider-Man to reveal who he is to her and kisses him, causing Peter to break down in tears, believing MJ has remembered him. However, a mysterious force has taken control of MJ's mind, using her to taunt Peter before compelling her to jump off of a rooftop, but she is saved by Peter and regains consciousness.
Peter takes MJ to Frank Castle's lair to hide out, where he explains that she had been possessed by a telepath named Jean Grey, who has been in conflict with Peter and targeted MJ due to her connection to him. MJ helps Peter develop two power inhibitors; one specifically for his mutating arachnid DNA, and a universal inhibitor for Jean. Peter departs shortly after to help the Department of Damage Control apprehend Jean, and MJ urges Castle to follow Peter and help him. While they are gone, MJ discovers the letter Peter wrote to her and Ned explaining the spell. When he returns, MJ confronts him about the letter. He explains himself and confesses his love for her, but she apologizes to him, saying that she truly has no memory of him and cannot reciprocate.

**Zendaya Maree Stoermer Coleman**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-3) (born September 1, 1996) is an American actress and singer.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-9) Known for her work in television, blockbuster films, and advertising, her accolades include two Primetime Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe Award. She has been featured on _Forbes_' 30 under 30 list and was named one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2022 by _Time_. Zendaya's films as a leading actress have grossed over $9.8 billion worldwide.
Born in Oakland, California, Zendaya began her career as a child model and dancer before gaining prominence for her roles on the Disney Channel sitcoms _Shake It Up_ (2010–2013) and _K.C. Undercover_ (2015–2018), the latter of which she also produced. For her performance as the drug-addicted teenager Rue Bennett in the HBO drama series _Euphoria_ (2019–2026), Zendaya was nominated for three Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series and won two, becoming the youngest performer to win the award.

Zendaya made her feature film debut as Michelle Jones-Watson in the Marvel Cinematic Universe film _Spider-Man: Homecoming_ (2017). She reprised the role in the film's sequels _Far From Home_ (2019), _No Way Home_ (2021), and _Brand New Day_ (2026). She also starred in the musical film _The Greatest Showman_ (2017), Denis Villeneuve's _Dune_ trilogy (2021–2026), and _The Odyssey_ (2026), and has earned praise for her performances in the romance films _Malcolm & Marie_ (2021), _Challengers_ (2024) and _The Drama_ (2026).
In 2013, Zendaya released the album _Zendaya_ with Hollywood Records. Its lead single, "Replay", peaked in the top 40 of the US _Billboard_ Hot 100 and earned multi-platinum certifications. "Rewrite the Stars", her duet with Zac Efron from the 2017 soundtrack for _The Greatest Showman_, charted in the top 20 and achieved multi-platinum status in various countries. Zendaya wrote the 2013 book _Between U and Me: How to Rock Your Tween Years with Style and Confidence_, and in 2021 she became the youngest person to win the CFDA Fashion Icon award at the CFDA Fashion Awards.

## Early life
Zendaya was born in Oakland, California.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-y873-10)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerricone202512-11) Her name derives from the Shona name _Tendai_ (meaning 'to give thanks').[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-12) Both of her parents were working as teachers at the time of her birth.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-t542-13) Her father, Kazembe Ajamu Coleman, is a black American with Nigerian ancestry.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-a422-14) Her mother, Claire Stoermer, has German and Scottish ancestry.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-comp1-15) Zendaya has six older half-siblings from her father's previous relationships: Latonja, Austin, Julien, Kaylee, Katianna and AnnaBella.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-g126-16) Zendaya's parents divorced in 2016.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-t542-13)

## Early life
Zendaya attended Fruitvale Elementary School in Oakland, where her mother taught.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJames202312-17) She was described as energetic and outgoing at home but reserved and shy at school. At the end of her first school year, her parents had her repeat kindergarten to help build her confidence.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerricone202512-11) Because of her father's passion for basketball, Zendaya's parents enrolled her in a local basketball team. After losing interest in the sport, she switched to soccer and track, but lost interest in those sports, too.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerricone202512%E2%80%9313-18) At age six, Zendaya and two of her friends—the only three Black children at the school—convinced the principal to let them perform a play for Black History Month.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-Field-2016-19)

## Career
### 2004–2009: Beginnings
At age eight, Zendaya joined Future Shock Oakland, a hip-hop dance group with which she performed for three years.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerricone202513-20)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-i769-21) She also spent two years dancing hula with the Academy of Hawaiian Arts.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJames20239-22)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerricone202543-23) After deciding to pursue acting, Zendaya assisted her mother, who spent the summer working as a house manager at the California Shakespeare Theater.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerricone202513-20) There, she assisted patrons with their seats and sold fundraising tickets, but her primary interest was in the performances.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJames202312-17)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-a460-24) Her first acting role was as a silkworm in her school's production of _James and the Giant Peach_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerricone202513-20) At age eleven, she began attending Oakland School for the Arts[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJames202312-17) and was cast in several roles in local theaters. Zendaya portrayed Little Ti Moune in _Once on This Island_ at the Berkeley Playhouse. She played Joe—a role originally written for a male performer—at TheaterWorks' Palo Alto production of _Caroline, or Change_.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerricone202514-25)

## Career
### 2009–2016: Disney Channel
In 2014, Zendaya appeared as a guest judge on an episode of _Project Runway: Under the Gunn_ in which contestants were challenged to design an outfit for her to wear at an upcoming concert performance.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-t804-67) In March 2015, musician Timbaland confirmed that he was collaborating with Zendaya on her second album, after her move from Disney's label to Republic Records.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-68) The following year, she released the single "Something New" featuring Chris Brown, through Hollywood Records and Republic Records.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-o654-69)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-s949-52) In December 2016, Zendaya appeared as a guest judge in the season finale of _Project Runway_'s 15th season.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-70)

## Career
### 2017–2021: Mature roles and breakthrough
Zendaya at the 2018 MTV Movie & TV Awards in Santa Monica, California
In 2017, Zendaya appeared in the music video for Bruno Mars's song "Versace on the Floor"[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-71) and made her feature film debut in the Marvel Cinematic Universe film _Spider-Man: Homecoming_ as Michelle "MJ" Jones-Watson.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-u490-72)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-73) She wore no makeup and regular clothes to her screen test; producers Kevin Feige and Amy Pascal did not recognize her despite her fame.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-j156-62)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-t002-63) Zendaya described Michelle as awkward, intellectual, and "very dry". She found it refreshing to play a character who was "weird" and "different", and believed that many young people—and especially young women—could relate to Michelle.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-HollywoodReporter-74)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-ZendayaDigitalSpy-75) Zendaya added her own embellishments to the character, including carrying around a mug of "strange" herbal tea.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-j156-62)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-t002-63)

## Career
### 2017–2021: Mature roles and breakthrough
_Spider-Man:_ _Homecoming_ grossed over $880 million worldwide, making it the sixth-highest-grossing film of 2017.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-c802-76) Critics at _The Hollywood Reporter_ and _The Guardian_ praised Zendaya as a "scene stealer",[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-77)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-g105-78) while Stephanie Zacharek of _Time_ lauded her "delightfully sullen insouciance".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-q076-79) Zendaya then starred in the musical film _The Greatest Showman_ (2017), portraying a trapeze artist who falls in love with a white man (Zac Efron) during a time when interracial relationships were socially taboo.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-y294-80)Owen Gleiberman of _Variety_ praised her on-screen chemistry with Efron,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-81) while David Rooney of _The Hollywood Reporter_ said she brought "touching sensitivity" to her role.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-82) Zendaya appeared on three songs from the film's soundtrack, including "Rewrite the Stars" and "The Greatest Show", which reached numbers 70 and 88 respectively on _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-k265-83)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendaya#cite_note-u701-84)
Zendaya at the premiere of _Spider-Man: Far From Home_ in Hollywood, California in 2019

## Career

**Michelle Jones-Watson**, most commonly known as **MJ**, is a fictionalcharacter portrayed by Zendaya in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) film franchise, an original character within the media franchise that pays homage to Mary Jane "MJ" Watson, main love interest of Spider-Man in comic books and various media.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Zendaya1-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-4)

She is depicted as a smart, snarky classmate of Peter Parker in _Spider-Man: Homecoming_ (2017), and in _Spider-Man: Far From Home_ (2019) becomes his love interest as well as correctly guessing Peter is Spider-Man.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Geek-5) She returns in _Spider-Man: No Way Home_ (2021), helping Peter, Ned Leeds, and Doctor Strange to capture multiple villains that have entered their universe from the multiverse, due to a failed spell to make the world forget about Mysterio revealing that Peter was Spider-Man. Her romantic involvement in Peter's personal life would eventually be undone due to Strange's casting of a spell that permanently erased the world's memory of Peter's civilian persona, including the loss of his previous bonds he forged with his friends, loved ones, and allies.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-6) MJ returns in _Spider-Man: Brand New Day_ (2026), living a normal life after forgetting Peter. However, she is quickly caught in the middle of Peter's conflict with Jean Grey, where she discovers Spider-Man's identity and appears to regain her memories of Peter by the movie's end.
The character has received positive reviews, and Zendaya has been praised as a strong female supporting cast member, receiving the Saturn Award for Best Supporting Actress for her acting in _Far From Home_.

## Creation and concept
[edit]
> She has a really cool wardrobe, really funny, lots of literary nods. I like the idea that she's a real reader and bookish. She always has a big pile of books she's carrying around, which I picked and obsessed over.
According to _Spider-Man: Homecoming_ co-screenwriter John Francis Daley, Michelle was intended as a reinvention of Mary Jane Watson.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-yahoo!-8) While her nickname reveal was an homage to the supporting character within the comic books and other Spider-Man media, Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige confirmed she is an original Marvel Cinematic Universe character.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-IGN-9) Feige added: "Peter's had a lot of friends over the years in the comics, and a lot of schoolmates and characters he's interacted with. It wasn't just Mary Jane Watson; it wasn't just Gwen Stacy; it wasn't just Harry Osborn. So we were very interested in the other characters, and that's where Liz came from and that's where the version of the character Michelle came from."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-DOG-10)Jon Watts, director of _Spider-Man: Homecoming_, _Spider-Man: Far From Home_ and _Spider-Man: No Way Home_, likened the character to Ally Sheedy's Allison Reynolds from _The Breakfast Club_ (1985) and Linda Cardellini's Lindsay Weir from _Freaks and Geeks_ (1999–2000).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-\film-7)

Zendaya portrays the character in the MCU.
MJ is portrayed by actress Zendaya in the Marvel Cinematic Universe as a classmate of Peter Parker at Midtown School of Science and Technology and a teammate on the academic decathlon team. She is depicted as politically active with critical views, and a loner who claims to eschew friendship.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Mashable-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-CheatSheet-13) Zendaya described the character as "very dry, awkward, intellectual".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-HollywoodReporter-14) This sometimes manifests itself in the form of deadpan sarcasm,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Polygon-17) as when she calls Peter and Ned "losers" for ogling his crush, Liz, from afar.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-CheatSheet-13) Among her unusual hobbies is attending detention simply to "sketch people in crisis."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Mashable-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-CheatSheet-13)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-WhatCulture-18)

## Portrayal and characterization
Unlike previous supporting female characters within _Spider-Man_ films, such as Mary Jane Watson from the Sam Raimi trilogy and Gwen Stacy from the _Amazing Spider-Man_ films, MJ is neither a romantic interest nor a damsel in distress at the beginning of her character arc. Instead, the character Liz was created initially for the role of romantic interest in a way that tied into Parker's conflict with the Vulture.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-19)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-Geek-5)
In the third film, she is rescued from a fall by Andrew Garfield's incarnation of Spider-Man, prompting an emotional moment for that Spider-Man, in light of his failure to save Gwen Stacy from a similar fate in _The Amazing Spider-Man 2_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-rescue-20)

## Fictional character biography
[edit]
In 2016, Michelle, commonly known as MJ, is introduced as a student at Midtown School of Science and Technology and enjoys mocking her classmates, including Peter Parker. She is a member of the Academic Decathlon team and attends a competition in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), during which they win, although she notices Peter's disappearance. At the Washington Monument, she witnesses Spider-Man's arrival. After Liz Allan leaves the school, she is offered Allan's role of Captain of the team by Roger Harrington. She begins to open up more with teammates, such as Peter and Ned Leeds, secretly considering them as her friends.
In 2018, MJ is a victim of the Blip,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-21) before being restored to life in 2023.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-22) In 2024, MJ attends the school-sponsored trip to Europe, where her affections are sought out by both Peter and Brad Davis. When she deduces Peter's identity as Spider-Man, MJ helps discover Mysterio's hero fraud, as he was the one who staged the Elemental invasion. In London, MJ, Ned, Betty Brant, and Flash Thompson are met by Happy Hogan and take cover from Mysterio's drones after they get targeted. After Mysterio is defeated, MJ embraces Peter. Soon after returning home, MJ and Peter begin a relationship and have their first date by swinging in the city. Afterwards, they witness _TheDailyBugle.net_'sJ. Jonah Jameson releasing a doctored video of Mysterio and Spider-Man, claiming that Spider-Man is responsible for the Battle of London (during which Mysterio was killed) and exposing his identity as Peter Parker.

## Fictional character biography
### Multiversal invasion
[edit]
MJ is immediately surrounded by people asking her if she is Spider-Man's girlfriend, but is picked up by Peter and swung back to his apartment, where she meets Peter's aunt May. She is eventually interrogated and taken to custody by the Department of Damage Control. MJ, Peter, and Ned then become infamous, resulting in all their college applications being rejected.
MJ and Ned are found by Stephen Strange and brought to the New York Sanctum to help Peter track down individuals from alternate universes who were brought to theirs after a spell went wrong. They are instructed by Peter to keep watch over Strange's mystical box as he tries to help the individuals be cured of their villainous traits. At Ned's grandmother's house, MJ encourages Ned to use Strange's sling ring to try to locate Peter. Ned successfully opens a portal, but the two are instead met with an alternate version of Peter (later dubbed "Peter-Three"). Ned tries again, only to locate another alternate version of Peter (later dubbed "Peter-Two"). MJ and Ned go to Midtown's rooftop and comfort Peter, who had just witnessed the Green Goblin kill May. They then introduce him to his two variants, who provide advice, and join them in Midtown's laboratory.
MJ and Ned are attacked by Lizard after Ned is unable to close the portal from Midtown to the Statue of Liberty, although Peter comes to their aid. MJ and Ned escape onto the Statue and Ned opens another portal, this time leading them to Strange. MJ falls off of the statue after a pumpkin bomb from the Goblin detonates on the mystical box, destabilizing the spell once more and threatening the fabric of reality. Peter tries to save her but is whisked away by the Goblin, and Peter-Three, who lost his own girlfriend, Gwen Stacy, in a similar manner, takes notice and saves her. Peter tells MJ and Ned that Strange would recast the spell on his request to erase him from everyone's memory in order to send the multiversal visitors back home. MJ confesses her love for Parker and they kiss passionately before the spell takes effect.
Weeks later, MJ greets Ned at her shop, both having been accepted into MIT, and meets Peter, who considers reintroducing himself, but ultimately decides against it, wishing to not involve her and Ned in his life again to protect them from harm.

## Fictional character biography
### Multiversal invasion
After graduating from MIT, MJ and Ned rent an apartment together in New York. During the housewarming party, MJ runs into Peter, who had followed Ned into the apartment and mingled with the crowd. He had brought flowers with him, passing them off as a welcome gift and giving them to her, pretending to be a neighbor. Peter watches her from afar until he sees her with her new boyfriend, which compels him to leave.
Some time later, Spider-Man appears at MJ's apartment, saying she is in danger urging her to come with him, to which she reluctantly obliges. On a rooftop, MJ asks Spider-Man to reveal who he is to her and kisses him, causing Peter to break down in tears, believing MJ has remembered him. However, a mysterious force has taken control of MJ's mind, using her to taunt Peter before compelling her to jump off of a rooftop, but she is saved by Peter and regains consciousness.
Peter takes MJ to Frank Castle's lair to hide out, where he explains that she had been possessed by a telepath named Jean Grey, who has been in conflict with Peter and targeted MJ due to her connection to him. MJ helps Peter develop two power inhibitors; one specifically for his mutating arachnid DNA, and a universal inhibitor for Jean. Peter departs shortly after to help the Department of Damage Control apprehend Jean, and MJ urges Castle to follow Peter and help him. While they are gone, MJ discovers the letter Peter wrote to her and Ned explaining the spell. When he returns, MJ confronts him about the letter. He explains himself and confesses his love for her, but she apologizes to him, saying that she truly has no memory of him and cannot reciprocate.

It wasn't just Mary Jane Watson; it wasn't just Gwen Stacy; it wasn't just Harry Osborn. So we were very interested in the other characters, and that's where Liz came from and that's where the version of the character Michelle came from."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-DOG-10)Jon Watts, director of _Spider-Man: Homecoming_, _Spider-Man: Far From Home_ and _Spider-Man: No Way Home_, likened the character to Ally Sheedy's Allison Reynolds from _The Breakfast Club_ (1985) and Linda Cardellini's Lindsay Weir from _Freaks and Geeks_ (1999–2000).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe)#cite_note-\film-7)

MJ falls off of the statue after a pumpkin bomb from the Goblin detonates on the mystical box, destabilizing the spell once more and threatening the fabric of reality. Peter tries to save her but is whisked away by the Goblin, and Peter-Three, who lost his own girlfriend, Gwen Stacy, in a similar manner, takes notice and saves her. Peter tells MJ and Ned that Strange would recast the spell on his request to erase him from everyone's memory in order to send the multiversal visitors back home. MJ confesses her love for Parker and they kiss passionately before the spell takes effect.
Weeks later, MJ greets Ned at her shop, both having been accepted into MIT, and meets Peter, who considers reintroducing himself, but ultimately decides against it, wishing to not involve her and Ned in his life again to protect them from harm.
